items.name: Charger
items.description: War horses bred for strength and courage in battle. Adapted to short bursts of speed; not suited to long-distance riding.

items.name: Dapple-doff
items.description: Mighty, shaggy-furred draft horses, bred for their great strength. Dull-witted and easily spooked.

items.name: Hop-clopper
items.description: Stocky, green-maned draft horses beloved by Prigwort breweries. Get tetchy without their daily pint of ale.

items.name: Mule
items.description: Stubborn horse/donkey cross-breeds used as beasts of burden. Unlike other horses, mules can be taken underground.

items.name: Prigwort prancer
items.description: Lightly built horses adapted to run at high speed. Fond of snacking on acorns in the autumn.

items.name: Yellow-flank
items.description: Tall, slender horses favoured by nobility, with flowing, silver manes and golden dappling along their sides. The haughty, laughing neigh of the yellow-flank bespeaks the breed's rumoured fairy ancestry.

items.name: Feed (1 day)
items.description: A sack of hay, oat grains, and the odd apple or carrot to chomp.

items.name: Horse barding (+2 AC)
items.description: Armour made of leather and plates of metal. Grants a +2 bonus to Armour Class.

items.name: Pack saddle and bridle
items.description: A pack saddle is necessary for horses to carry heavy loads, as it includes a rack upon which to lash crates, bags, and bundles.

items.name: Riding saddle and bridle
items.description: A riding saddle is a leather seat required to mount and ride a horse.

items.name: Riding saddle bags
items.description: Hold up to 500 coins of weight.

items.name: Cart
items.description: A two-wheeled vehicle. If pulled by twice as many animals (2 draft horses or 4 mules), a cart can hold up to 20,000 coins of weight.

items.name: Wagon
items.description: A four-wheeled, open vehicle. If pulled by twice as many animals (4 draft horses or 8 mules), a wagon can hold up to 40,000 coins of weight.

items.name: Barge
items.description: A flat-bottomed boat, 20′ long and 10′ wide, designed for carrying cargo. Barges may be rowed, pushed with poles, or pulled by horses on the riverbank.

items.name: Canoe
items.description: A small boat, 15′ long and 3′ wide, made of hide or canvas stretched over a wooden frame. Because of its small size and lightweight construction (weighing 500 coins), a canoe may be carried by two people.

items.name: Fishing boat
items.description: A small sailing boat, 20–30′ long and 6′ wide.

items.name: Raft
items.description: A professionally built raft has raised sides, a basic steering oar, and some form of shelter for goods or passengers. Such a raft may be up to 30′ × 40′. Professionally built rafts are sometimes floated downstream with cargo and then broken down and sold for the value of their wood (25cp per square foot).

items.name: Raft, makeshift
items.description: Given sufficient trees for wood, characters may build a makeshift raft in 1d3 days per 10′ square section (up to a maximum size of 20′ × 30′).

items.name: Rowing boat
items.description: A small wooden boat for 1–2 people, 10′ long and 4′ wide.
